source_text: XVIII. Ἰδὼν οὖν ὁ κεντυρίων τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων γενομένην φιλονεικίαν, θεὶς αὐτὸν ἐν μέσῳ, ὡς ἔθος αὐτοῖς, ἔκαυσεν. Οὕτως τε ἡμεῖς ὕστερον ἀνελόμενοι τὰ τιμιώτερα λίθων πολυτελῶν καὶ δοκιμώτερα ὑπὲρ χρυσίον ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ, ἀπεθέμεθα ὅπου καὶ ἀκόλουθον ἦν. Ἔνθα ὡς δυνατὸν ἡμῖν συναγομένοις ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ χαρᾷ παρέξει ὁ κύριος ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου αὐτοῦ ἡμέραν γενέθλιον, εἴς τε τὴν τῶν προηθληκότων μνήμην καὶ τῶν μελλόντων ἄσκησίν τε καὶ ἑτοιμασίαν.
pass_a_gloss: Since the centurion saw the strife that had come about on the part of the Jews, he put him in the middle and burned him, as is custom with them; and thus we afterward, having picked up his bones, more honored than costly stones and more approved than gold, laid them away where it was also fitting; where, as far as possible for us gathering together in exultation and joy, the Lord will give to carry out the birthday of his martyrdom, both for the memory of those who contended before and for the discipline and preparation of those about to come.
pass_b_english: When the centurion saw the bitter dispute that had arisen among the Jews, he placed him in the midst and burned him, as is their custom. So afterward we took up his bones, more precious than costly stones and more tried than gold, and laid them where it was fitting.

There, as far as lies with us when we gather in exultation and joy, the Lord will grant us to celebrate the birthday of his martyrdom, both for the remembrance of those who have already wrestled and for the training and preparation of those to come.

choices.reason: contention embittered over the body, not a mere quarrel
